raw_response:
I've been working this land for more than fifty years. My husband is gone now, my sons moved to Shijiazhuang and Beijing long ago. I manage the fields myself, though I hire the village machinery cooperative to do the mechanized work — planting, harvesting — I can't do that anymore with my back.

My land is about 5 mu. The plots my family has always farmed. I don't think about changing. The soil here is good for wheat and corn. That's what we grow. That's what the village grows. That's what the grain station wants to buy.

In October I'll put winter wheat in. I'll use the seed from the township seed shop — same improved kind I've used for years, everyone buys it. Before seeding I'll have the rotary tiller come through. I put down the compound fertilizer and diammonium phosphate all at once as base fertilizer, then in March I spread urea by hand when the weather turns. I pump water from the well — before winter sets in, again in early spring at jointing, again when it heads, sometimes once more if it's dry. Three or four times. Wheat needs the water here in Hebei or it doesn't fill properly.

After wheat harvest in June, the corn goes in right away — no time to waste. The machine does direct seeding right into the stubble. Corn is a hybrid, same one as last year, you can't save seed from hybrid. Corn grows through the summer rains mostly. I irrigate maybe twice if it's dry. I apply fertilizer at planting and then again when it's waist high.

I keep a small corner near the house — garlic, scallions, a few vegetables for the pot. Not worth counting in the plan.

I will do exactly what I always do. At 74, I'm not experimenting.
